paper_metadata.title: Fracture of vanadium alloys under impact and tensile conditions at low temperatures

evidence.quote: A comparative study of the low-temperature fracture characteristics of V – Cr – W – Zr and V – Cr – Ta – Zr vanadium alloys under impact and tension conditions was performed.
A comparative study of the low-temperature fracture characteristics of V – Cr – W – Zr and V – Cr – Ta – Zr vanadium alloys under impact and tension conditions was performed.
V – Cr – W – Zr alloy
V – Cr – Ta – Zr alloy

The V – Cr – Ta – Zr alloy, even after thermal stabilization at 1323 K, due to the uniform distribution of nano-sized particles ( Fig. 1 f), retains a finely crystalline state ( Fig. 1 d) with elements of a polygonal structure ( Fig. 1 e).

In the case of the V – Cr – W – Zr alloy studied in this work, alloying with tungsten leads to inhomogeneity of the grain ( Fig. 1 a), subgrain (polygonal) ( Fig. 1 b) and disperse heterophase ( Fig. 1 c) structure, which negatively affects the ductility, especially at cryogenic temperature, and similarly affects the impact toughness.
